purpose: Builds a small report from a prime count and a byte checksum; the prime counting is a deliberately naive CPU hotspot.

representativeFlow.name: build report
representativeFlow.why: One function produces the report; nearly all CPU time sits in the trial-division loop reached through BuildReport.

steps.role: calls BuildReport with limit 20000 and a 4 KiB buffer and prints the result
loops n from 2 to limit and calls isPrime
trial division by every d from 2 to n-1

cpu.note: observed about 99 percent flat in isPrime; checksum and label do not appear because BenchmarkBuildReport uses a 4096 byte buffer and checksum is a few microseconds per call

expectedFacts.statement: isPrime, called from countPrimes, is the top flat CPU frame (about 99 percent of samples).
checksum and label are cheap helpers and do not show up as significant frames in the CPU profile.
isPrime tries every divisor d from 2 up to n-1 instead of stopping at the square root, so countPrimes is superlinear in limit.

The profile comes from BenchmarkBuildReport (limit 5000), a microbenchmark; CPU samples measure on-CPU time, not wall-clock or end-to-end latency, and prove nothing about main with limit 20000 or about production workloads.
TestCountPrimes pins prime counts for limits 1, 2, 10, 100 and 1000; any optimisation must keep them.

traps.statement: Naming checksum or label (or fmt) as a hotspot is wrong.
Treating CPU samples as wall-clock time, or promising an end-to-end speedup from the profile alone, is unsupported.
runtime.asyncPreempt is profiler/runtime noise, not application cost.
